subject: Archaeology
title: Hiram Bingham Reaches Machu Picchu
description: A short lesson to help you apply Hiram Bingham Reaches Machu Picchu.

hook.text: In 1911, a Yale professor hacked through jungle and climbed a mountain in Peru. He found a lost Inca city.

buildup.text: Hiram Bingham was searching for Vilcabamba, the last Inca stronghold. A local farmer led him up instead.

discovery.text: At 8,000 feet, Bingham found stone terraces, temples, and fountains hidden under centuries of jungle growth.

twist.text: Bingham was not the first. Local farmers knew about the ruins and had been farming the terraces for years.

climax.text: He shipped thousands of artifacts to Yale. Peru fought for their return and finally got them back in 2012.

punchline.text: The 'discoverer' was led there by people who already knew.

quiz.question: Who actually knew about Machu Picchu before Bingham arrived?
options: Spanish conquistadors had mapped it centuries earlier
Local farmers had been using the terraces for years
A rival expedition had published a report the year before

details.summary: In 1911, American explorer Hiram Bingham reached Machu Picchu, a 15th-century Inca citadel perched at 2,430 meters in the Peruvian Andes. Though local farmers knew of its existence, Bingham's expedition brought it to international attention. It is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
details.whyItMatters: Machu Picchu combines sophisticated stone architecture, astronomical alignments, and agricultural terracing in a dramatic mountain setting. It demonstrates Inca engineering mastery and has become a global symbol of archaeological wonder.
takeaways: A 15th-century Inca citadel at 2,430 meters in the Andes
Hiram Bingham brought it to international attention in 1911
Demonstrates Inca mastery of stone architecture and engineering

faq.question: What was Machu Picchu's purpose?
faq.answer: Most scholars believe it was a royal estate for the Inca emperor Pachacuti, used as a retreat and ceremonial center. Its temples, astronomical observation points, and agricultural terraces suggest both religious and practical functions. It housed perhaps 750 people at its peak.

faq.question: Why was Machu Picchu abandoned?
faq.answer: The Spanish conquest disrupted the Inca empire in the 1530s. Without the imperial system to supply and maintain it, the remote citadel was abandoned. The Spanish never found it, which preserved it from the destruction they inflicted on other Inca sites.
